newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee sees more defective nuclear fuel rods.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee sees more defective nuclear fuel rods.

text.p: Maine Yankee Atomic Power Co said it has identified seven defective fuel assemblies at the 910 megawatt nuclear power plant, exceeding original expectations of four to six defective fuel rods.
About half of the 217 fuel assemblies at the plant had been inspected and all of the assemblies will have been reviewed by early next week, Maine Yankee said Friday in a statement.
The updated findings have been reported to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, the company said, adding that the assemblies most likely to contain defects were targeted for review first.
The plant, located in Wiscasset, Maine, was shut December 6, 1996 to review electrical cables and was expected to resume operation in mid-February, Maine Yankee said.

The plant is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
